claims.text: Adding about 2 at.% Hf to nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 will suppress Cr-V-rich precipitate formation under irradiation up to 8 dpa.
Hf addition will alter defect kinetics and stabilize grain-boundary chemistry.
The initial W38Ta36Cr15V11 material has a homogeneous nanoscale grain structure.
Ta, Cr, and V are uniformly distributed in the initial material.
Controlled-atmosphere powder processing can produce uniform Hf dispersion in the W-alloy matrix and at its grain boundaries while preventing oxidation.
The modified alloy will contain uniformly dispersed Hf atoms, and potentially nanometric Hf-based oxide dispersoids, at grain boundaries and within the matrix.
Dispersed Hf species will minimize local chemical inhomogeneities.
Dispersed Hf species will act as efficient defect and solute traps.
Hf will segregate to grain boundaries in irradiated nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11.
Grain-boundary Hf segregation will reduce the mobility and clustering tendency of Cr and V.
Reduced Cr and V mobility and clustering will disrupt nucleation of Cr-V-rich precipitates.
Approximately 2 at.% Hf will not significantly damage the nanocrystalline structure.
After irradiation, the Hf-modified alloy will show a marked reduction or near-absence of Cr-V-rich precipitates relative to the unmodified alloy.
After irradiation, the Hf-modified alloy will have a lower dislocation-loop density than the unmodified alloy.
Irradiation-induced hardening in the Hf-modified alloy will be comparable to or lower than that of the unmodified alloy.
Unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 forms Cr-V-rich precipitates near 8 dpa.
Unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits increased hardening near 8 dpa.
Unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 develops dislocation loops near 8 dpa.
The proposed precipitate suppression is limited to doses no greater than 8 dpa and specimen temperatures below 600°C.
At higher doses or temperatures, thermal instabilities or phase transformations may prevent precipitate suppression.

contradictions.description: The baseline is said to exhibit increased hardening near 8 dpa, whereas the desired comparison is framed as preserving the baseline alloy's low hardening. This makes the reference hardening state internally inconsistent.

Processing is intended to prevent oxidation, yet potential Hf-based oxide dispersoids are included as part of the proposed mediator, while unintended Hf-based secondary phases are also defined as a falsifying result. The acceptable versus falsifying role of Hf oxides is therefore unclear.
